name: Aelsin Ube-Coconut Mood Pearls
description: Small, spherical hard candies with an ube-violet shell encasing a liquid coconut center dosed with low-grade anxiolytic bioactive compounds. Sold in apothecary-style glass vials of fifteen.
flavor_profile: Sweet, earthy ube dissolving into a cool coconut cream with a subtle warmth as the bioactive compound takes effect — mild calm onset within twelve minutes
cultural_context: Aelsin Mood Pearls occupy a precise market niche: legal, mild emotional modulation for Tier 3-4 consumers who want something more discreet than a prescription and more effective than tea. The glass vial packaging is considered elegant and is frequently reused for storing jewelry, micro-components, or other small valuables.
story_hooks: Aelsin's anxiolytic compound is derived from a geneware-modified plant strain that a Tier 1 botanist developed and never received credit or compensation for — she wants the formula, the credit, or both.

A Tier 4 corporate negotiator has been secretly dosing a rival's coffee with crushed Mood Pearls before high-stakes meetings — the rival has noticed they feel unusually compliant but can't pinpoint why.
The Meridian 88 Pharmacological Oversight Bureau is preparing to reclassify Mood Pearls as a controlled substance; Aelsin's lobbyists are scrambling, and the company needs public-facing allies fast.
